jessica_pm: Kicking off a quick planning thread for Reserved Pools tiering and burst/fallback behavior. We need a minimally viable launch plan + must-have OKRs. Thoughts?
aj_eng: My high-level: two SLA tiers (standard / premium). Standard = best-effort 99th latency target, premium = committed p95/p99 and capacity reservations.
kyle_sre: Agree on two tiers. Need to clarify isolation boundaries: soft isolation (weighted fair share) vs hard isolation (dedicated nodes). Hard isolation = predictable but expensive.
jessica_pm: Customers ask for "guaranteed throughput" during spikes. Is that quota reservation or pre-warmed burst pool?
aj_eng: Technically cheaper to implement a burst pool that can be throttled and reclaimed. Reservation requires capacity commitment or strict admission control.
olga_research: Also call out model variants: fallback to smaller/quantized model during sustained overload. That preserves latency SLOs at some quality loss.
matt_sales: Several enterprise prospects asked for 99.9% availability + isolation. They'll pay for dedicated nodes but want autoscale to kick in before degradation.
jk? (typo) kyle_sre: :thumbsup: We should define concrete launch criteria: 1) Tier definitions + pricing doc agreed, 2) Autoscale policy prototype, 3) Canary tests + chaos runbook, 4) Documentation for customers.
aj_eng: For autoscale policy prototype, propose simple rules first: "scale_up_on_util>=85% for X mins" and "scale_down_cooldown=10m". Example config: ```json
{"policy": "util_based", "scale_up_threshold": 0.85, "min_replicas": 2, "max_replicas": 20, "cooldown_secs": 600}
```
jessica_pm: What's the expected warm-up time for a new replica? That affects how aggressive we should be.
aj_eng: Cold start for a large model ~ 60-90s to be warm for p95. Smaller quantized variant ~ 10-15s. That means burst pool + warm standby matters.
kyle_sre: Proposal: keep a tiny warm standby buffer per tenant in premium (configurable, default 1 replica) + shared global burst pool for short spikes. If burst pool exhausted, fallback ordering: 1) route to quantized variant 2) degrade non-critical requests 3) reject.
olga_research: Need to measure quality delta when falling back to quantized models. Add evals to OKR so we can quantify customer impact.
matt_sales: For launch messaging, we should be explicit about behavior during extreme overload. Customers hate opaque throttling.
deploy-bot: deploy:autoscale-prototype started by aj_eng at 2025-09-22T14:12:02Z
aj_eng: For SLAs, we need to decide on financial or non-financial first. Financial SLAs require measurement + billing pipeline hooks. That increases scope.
jessica_pm: Let's scope MFV (minimum feasible): non-financial SLA badging + precise SLO dashboards. Financial SLA as follow-up for top-tier enterprise. OK?
kyle_sre: OK. Also add stress tests to verify fallback ordering: simulate 3x expected qps for 20m, observe routing and latency. We need clear pass/fail criteria.
aj_eng: Pass criteria suggestion: premium p95 latency < target or fallback executed within 30s, no error rate > 0.5%.
olga_research: Add automatic quality regression alerts tied to fallback events (eval on sampled responses).
jessica_pm: Great. Can someone draft a launch checklist with owners? I'll assemble in the product board.
matt_sales: I'll own customer comms + pricing sketch.
kyle_sre: I'll own chaos/stress runs + runbook.
aj_eng: I'll build the autoscale prototype + burst pool integration.
olga_research: I'll own fallback evals and quantized quality metrics.
jessica_pm: Timeline idea: prototype + docs in 4 weeks, canary in 6 weeks, GA for pilot customers in 10-12 weeks. Any blockers?
matt_sales: Need legal review for any SLA wording (esp. non-financial claims).
kyle_sre: Need access to a staging reserved pool and ability to inject load across tenants.
aj_eng: One more tech note: ensure KV cache warmup isn't lost when switching variants — consider seamless KV migration or prefix-based caching.
jessica_pm: Awesome. I'll capture actions: Owners + due dates, and set a follow-up sync next Tue. Thanks all.
